title: There Is No One 'Disability Experience'
assessmentMethod: Private reflective journal entry, not scored

body.en: A wheelchair user, a Deaf person, someone with low vision, and someone with a cognitive disability can all be affected by the exact same flood — but not in the same way, and not needing the same response. A wheelchair user might need a route without stairs. A Deaf person needs a visual alert, not just a siren. Someone with low vision needs high-contrast, well-lit signage, not just a printed notice. Treating 'persons with disabilities' as one group with one set of needs is its own kind of oversight. Think of someone you know, or know of, whose specific needs during an emergency would look different from everyone else's around them. What would actually help them, specifically?
